key: Repel evil with that which is better. We are Best Aware of that which they allege.
s: Late in Al-Mu’minun, after a plea not to be counted among the wrongdoers, the Prophet receives a rule of conduct; Ibn Kathir, on 23:93 to 23:98, reads it as the antidote for life among people, good done to the wrongdoer until enmity turns to friendship.

evidence.words: ثُمَّ قَالَ مُرْشِدًا لَهُ إِلَى التِّرْياق النَّافِعِ فِي مُخَالَطَةِ النَّاسِ، وَهُوَ الْإِحْسَانُ إِلَى مَنْ يُسِيءُ، لِيَسْتَجْلِبَ خَاطِرَهُ، فَتَعُودُ عَدَاوَتُهُ صَدَاقَةً وَبُغْضُهُ مَحَبَّةً، فَقَالَ: ﴿ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ السَّيِّئَةَ﴾
evidence.gloss: Then He said, guiding him to the beneficial antidote in dealing with people, which is doing good to the one who does ill, so as to win his heart, until his enmity turns to friendship and his hatred to love: ‘Repel evil with that which is better.’

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Mu’minun 23:96, at 2768). Ibn Kathir, in his single comment on 23:93 to 23:98, says in his own voice that God then guided the Prophet to the beneficial antidote in dealing with people: doing good to the one who does ill, to win him, so that enmity turns to friendship and hatred to love; the reading is his and the place right. CHANGED the context clause only: the proposal placed the ayah ‘between the Prophet’s prayers for refuge’, but 23:93 to 23:94 is a plea not to be set among the wrongdoing folk, and both refuge prayers (23:97 to 23:98) come after it, so the ayah is not between them; now ‘after a plea not to be counted among the wrongdoers, the Prophet receives a rule of conduct’. Note for the record: al-Tabari, al-Qurtubi and the Jalalayn add that this forbearance toward the idolaters came before the command to fight (al-Qurtubi: abrogated as to the unbelievers, standing among believers); Ibn Kathir sets no such limit, and the sentence attributes nothing beyond his words. 45 words; entry-check ok.
